materials.caption: prompt:Image Details & Composition Layers ​The image is clearly divided into three distinct panels or layers, each offering a different perspective of the man and the car: ​1. Top Layer: The Driver's Reflection (Close-up) ​Subject: The man's face and torso, reflected in the driver's side wing mirror of the car. ​Action/Pose: He is seated inside the car (or just beyond the mirror's perspective), looking forward/slightly to the side with a serious expression. ​Attire: He is wearing a black leather jacket over a black shirt, and black sunglasses. His hair is styled in a typical dramatic, full manner. ​Car Detail: The interior visible in the reflection is a contrasting orange/tan leather. The mirror housing itself is highly in focus, framing the subject. ​Focus/Depth: Shallow depth of field (Bokeh). The mirror and the reflection are sharply in focus, while the background (likely the building) is significantly blurred. ​Camera Angle: Appears to be a Close-up shot, focused on the side mirror, taken from slightly in front and above the mirror's level. ​2. Middle Layer: Full Figure and Car (Mid-shot) ​Subject: The man standing next to the entire side profile of the black sports car. ​Action/Pose: He is leaning against the car with a relaxed but powerful posture, arms crossed over his chest, one leg slightly bent. ​Attire: The same black leather jacket and sunglasses, paired with dark grey or black jeans and brown leather boots. ​Car Detail: Shows the complete profile of the car (resembling a Bugatti Chiron). The car is entirely black with black wheels and aggressive styling. ​Setting: A paved, outdoor urban or industrial environment, with modern, blocky grey and white apartment/office buildings in the background. The lighting suggests an overcast day or shaded area. ​Focus/Depth: Medium depth of field. Both the man and the car are sharp, with the background buildings moderately in focus, establishing the environment. ​Camera Angle: A Medium Shot/Full Shot taken at eye level or slightly lower to emphasize the car's presence and the man's dominance in the frame. ​3. Bottom Layer: Car Rear (Low Angle) ​Subject: The rear view of the black sports car. ​Car Detail: Focuses on the distinctive rear taillights (two prominent horizontal red LED strips) and the rear diffuser/exhaust setup. A faint watermark is visible on the bumper: "Protosh_foture". ​Setting: The same urban/industrial background, showing more of the paved ground texture. ​Focus/Depth: Medium depth of field. The car is the primary focus, with the background buildings receding slightly. ​Camera Angle: A Low-Angle Shot (Worm's-eye view) taken from slightly below the car's bumper level, looking up. This angle makes the car appear more aggressive, powerful, and larger. ​🎨 Color Tones and Aesthetic ​Dominant Color Palette: Monochromatic/Desaturated. The primary colors are black, dark grey, and white/concrete grey. ​Mood: The overall aesthetic is sleek, powerful, and edgy. The heavy use of black on the car and the man's outfit creates a very noir or sophisticated action/thriller mood. ​Contrast: High visual contrast between the glossy black surfaces of the car and the matte/textured grey of the surrounding environment (pavement and buildings). ​Accents: The only warm color breaks are the brown leather boots in the middle panel and the orange/tan car interior reflected in the top panel, providing minor points of visual interest.#trending #vijay #fyp #aiprompt #ai

Prompt 📍

A hyper-realistic, high-key professional studio wedding photograph of an Indian couple in a romantic, intimate embrace. The background is pure, blown-out white, creating an ethereal, dreamy atmosphere.
The Subjects:
The Groom: Wearing a cream-colored silk Kurta. He has a beard and is wearing a traditional gold thread 'Bashikam' on his forehead.
The Bride: Wearing a peach and gold Kanjeevaram silk saree. Her blouse features heavy 'maggam' work embroidery with beads and stones on the sleeves. Her hair is braided and thickly adorned with fresh white jasmine flowers. She is wearing traditional gold jewelry including a matha patti, nose ring, heavy earrings, and a choker. Her hands have henna (mehndi) and are stacked with red and gold bangles.
The Garlands: Both are wearing matching, heavy wedding garlands made of pink lotus buds and green foliage.
The Pose: They are hugging closely, standing side-by-side in profile. Their foreheads are touching, eyes are closed, and they are sharing a gentle, happy smile.
Lighting & Style: Soft, diffused studio lighting. There is strong rim lighting (backlight) creating a glowing halo effect on their hair and shoulders. The image has a soft focus with a slight light flare/haze at the bottom right, replicating a professional photography style.

materials.creator: thecitizentz
materials.caption:
A new University of California, Berkeley study suggests that artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT are making it easier for students to obtain top grades in university, while also reducing the value of those grades for employers assessing graduates’ abilities.

The research, which analysed more than 500,000 grades across courses before and after ChatGPT’s release, found that classes heavily reliant on writing and coding saw a sharp rise in A grades. 

Professors in these AI-exposed subjects awarded about 30 percent more A’s, while fewer A-minus and B-plus grades were recorded, indicating a shift in grade distributions rather than improved learning outcomes. 

Researchers argue the pattern suggests students may be using generative AI to complete assignments more effectively, particularly in unsupervised, homework-based tasks. This, they say, risks inflating grades without necessarily improving understanding or skill levels. 

The findings raise concerns for employers, who increasingly rely on grade point averages to evaluate graduates. If AI tools are significantly influencing academic performance, grades may become a less reliable indicator of genuine ability in writing, coding and analytical tasks.

Educators are responding by redesigning assessments, increasing in-person examinations and reducing reliance on take-home work to better capture independent student learning.
